title: A local relation matrix fixing an irredundant tuple is invertible
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative local ring, meaning a commutative ring with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $n\ge0$ be an integer. Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in R$ be irredundant: for every $j$, there are no $c_i\in R$ with $a_j=\sum_{i\ne j}a_i c_i$. Let $B=(b_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ matrix over $R$ [def-weil-matrix] such that $a_j=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i b_{ij}$ for every $j$. Then $1-b_{jj}\in\mathfrak m$ and $b_{jj}$ is a unit for every $j$, while $b_{ij}\in\mathfrak m$ whenever $i\ne j$. Moreover, the determinant [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] $\det B$ is a unit, and $B$ is invertible: there is an $n\times n$ matrix $V$ over $R$ with $BV=VB=I_n$. A unit of $R$ means an element $u$ admitting $v\in R$ with $uv=1$.

proof.text:
Fix $j$. Rearranging the given relation gives $(1-b_{jj})a_j=\sum_{i
e j}a_i b_{ij}$. If $1-b_{jj}$ were a unit with inverse $v$, then $a_j=\sum_{i
e j}a_i(vb_{ij})$, contradicting irredundancy at $j$. The local-ring unit criterion therefore gives $1-b_{jj}\in\mathfrak m$. If also $b_{jj}\in\mathfrak m$, closure of the ideal under addition would give $1\in\mathfrak m$, impossible for a maximal ideal. Thus $b_{jj}
otin\mathfrak m$ and the same criterion makes $b_{jj}$ a unit.

proof.text: Fix $i\ne j$. If $b_{ij}$ were a unit with inverse $v$, the same column relation would give $a_i=a_jv(1-b_{jj})-\sum_{k\ne i,j}a_kvb_{kj}$. This expresses $a_i$ as a linear combination of the other tuple entries, contrary to irredundancy at $i$. Hence $b_{ij}$ is not a unit, and the local-ring unit criterion gives $b_{ij}\in\mathfrak m$. No cancellation by an $a_i$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, final paragraph, lines 20672–20680; expanded coefficient and determinant arguments

proof.text: Use the Leibniz formula for $\det B$. Each nonidentity permutation $\sigma$ moves some $k$, so its product has the factor $b_{\sigma(k),k}\in\mathfrak m$ by Step 2; that signed product lies in $\mathfrak m$. The identity-permutation term is $\prod_j b_{jj}$. Write $b_{jj}=1+u_j$ with $u_j\in\mathfrak m$ by Step 1. Expanding the finite product, every term of $\prod_j(1+u_j)-1$ contains a factor $u_j$, so it too belongs to $\mathfrak m$. Adding these terms proves $\det B-1\in\mathfrak m$. If $\det B$ belonged to $\mathfrak m$, subtracting $\det B-1$ would put $1$ in this proper ideal. Thus $\det B\notin\mathfrak m$ and the unit criterion makes it a unit. This also covers $n=0$: the determinant formula gives the empty product $1$ and there are no nonidentity terms.

source.place: Tag 0592, lemma-projective-freeness-criteria, final paragraph, lines 20672–20680; expanded coefficient and determinant arguments

proof.text: Choose $d\in R$ with $d\det B=1$, which is possible by Step 3 and commutativity. Let $V=d\operatorname{adj}(B)$. The adjugate identity states $B\operatorname{adj}(B)=\operatorname{adj}(B)B=(\det B)I_n$. Scalar multiplication commutes with matrix multiplication over the commutative ring $R$, as follows entrywise from distributivity in each finite row-column sum. Consequently $BV=d(B\operatorname{adj}(B))=I_n$ and $VB=d(\operatorname{adj}(B)B)=I_n$. For $n=0$ these are equalities of empty matrices.
